Club Refrigeration CC has operated since 1976 as South Africa's leading cleanroom manufacturer, running from a fully owned 10,000 square metre site in Rosslyn, Pretoria, with a long-serving, well-trained permanent workforce backed by qualified sub-contractors. The company offers full turnkey services for industrial-scale projects, from design and specialist engineering through manufacture, installation and ongoing repairs and maintenance, covering cleanrooms and GMP facilities, air handling units, fire-rated panels and doors, cannabis processing plants, post-harvest cooling, and mortuaries.

An active research and development programme has produced several products later copied across the industry, including its tongue-and-groove panel jointing system, flashing profiles and extrusions, and sliding door hardware. Club Refrigeration positions its approach around thorough consultation to identify each customer's specific needs before offering an economically viable solution, serving pharmaceutical, agricultural and food industry clients who need controlled environments built to a precise specification rather than off-the-shelf.

EXAH is a Salesforce and MuleSoft consulting and implementation partner based in Waterkloof, Pretoria, with a second office in Stellenbosch and clients across Africa, the Middle East and Europe in sectors including fintech, healthcare, consumer goods and manufacturing. Founded in 2014, the firm built its practice around Marketing, Sales, FinTech, Customer Service and Commerce solutions on the Salesforce platform, growing to around 40 staff.

Salesforce named EXAH its Overall Implementation Partner of the Year for Sub-Saharan Africa for three consecutive years, from 2021 to 2023, recognition that reflects its standing within the Salesforce partner ecosystem. In October 2025, EXAH was acquired by NTT Data, a move intended to combine EXAH's regional Salesforce expertise with NTT Data's global capabilities and strategic partnerships, giving its existing clients access to a larger international network while keeping its Pretoria base.

S and P Power Units has more than 30 years of experience in renewable energy and power supply, having installed over 7,500 systems across Southern Africa, Sub-Saharan Africa and Eastern Africa. The company designs, supplies and installs off-grid and grid-tied solar and backup power solutions for commercial, residential and agricultural clients, tailoring each system to the client's specific power needs rather than offering a single standard setup.

Alongside full system installation, S and P Power Units repacks batteries for cordless appliances such as power tools, radios and shavers, using higher-capacity 2,200 mA/h cells that last longer between charges than most original batteries. The business also stocks a wide range of power supply products including inverters, charge controllers, chargers, converters, gel and alkaline batteries, and surge protection, positioned as a one-stop power solution shop for both new installations and keeping existing battery-powered equipment running.

Rathusa Glass & Aluminium has worked in the glass and aluminium industry for 14 years, supplying and installing windows and doors including uPVC, steel, wooden and aluminium frames, double-glazed units, and sliding or folding doors. As a member of the South African Glazing and Glaziers Association (SAGGA), the business adheres to the industry's code of conduct, and has carried out extensive glazing work on RDP and GAP housing projects as well as for other major companies and government institutions.

The business describes itself as supplying glass to people rather than buildings, and emphasises direct interaction with clients to get each job made to their specific requirements. Rathusa Glass & Aluminium, based in East Lynne, Pretoria, trades Monday to Friday from 8am to 4:30pm, and its mix of residential custom glazing and larger institutional housing project work suits both homeowners and government-linked contractors needing glass and aluminium fitted to a precise specification.

Woodhill Country Club's golf course sits on a former dairy farm in the south-eastern suburbs of Pretoria, designed by Peter Matkovich and built to retain the site's old pastoral charm even as the residential estate around it grew up. The parklands layout plays over Kikuyu fairways and bent-grass greens across a front nine that rises and circles 'the hill' before flattening into a more heavily wooded back nine, running to a total length of 6,752 metres with a choice of three tee options.

The course hosted the PGA Championship in 2001, a measure of its standing among South African parkland courses, and its facilities include a clubhouse, driving range, pro shop, teaching academy and locker rooms. Visitors are welcome at Woodhill Country Club, though not on Saturday mornings, and the club advises booking tee times and any nearby accommodation ahead to avoid disappointment during busier periods.
